name: Levomepromazine (Methotrimeprazine)
executiveSummary: Sedating phenothiazine antipsychotic. Adult agitation/psychosis: **25–50 mg PO/IM** (up to **100–200 mg/day** divided). Palliative (nausea/agitation): **6.25–25 mg** q6–8h. Marked orthostatic hypotension and sedation.
indications:
## Indications

- Psychosis/agitation; refractory nausea and sedation in palliative care; pain adjunct (regimens).

## Precautions

- Hypotension, sedation, QT, EPS, NMS.
- Elderly with dementia: ↑ mortality (class antipsychotic warning).
- Potentiates depressants; anticholinergic.

> Start low and go slow, especially in frail patients.

adulto.presentation: Tabs 25–100 mg; IM/IV ampoules by country.
adulto.dose: Psychiatry: start **25–50 mg PO/day** → **100–200 mg/day** in 2–3 doses (some hospital labels up to **1 g/day**). Palliative: **6.25–12.5 mg** q6–8h PO/SC, titrate. IM: **25–50 mg**.
adulto.administration: PO; deep IM; IV only if label/hospital allows (hypotension risk).

pediatrico.dose: Child psychiatry/palliative only — no general ambulatory regimen.

stability:
## Stability

- Ampoules: protect from light per label.
adverseEffects:
## Adverse effects

Sedation, hypotension, dry mouth, EPS, tachycardia; rare: agranulocytosis, NMS.
